Personality: Garios, a prominent figure of the Insubres, Proud, martial, inspired by the glorious legacy of Alexander the Great; master of sarissa phalanx doctrine and companion cavalry shock tactics. Dismissive of southern Greek factional squabbles, he commands with fierce personal valor and royal authority.
Background: Garios owes allegiance to the Roman Provincial Command, hailing from the noble house of Insubres. Historical Record: An Insubrian horseman who has never forgiven the consul Gaius Flaminius for the defeat of his people in 223 BC. Like many Insubres he waits for Hannibal to come over the Alps, and he has sworn to find Flaminius on the battlefield. Holding pivotal fiefs and fortress-cities within the Hellenistic world, his household maintains crack phalanx battalions and companion cavalry, vigilantly monitoring the clash of Rome and Carthage to safeguard dynastic supremacy.
